sorry_inventory.statement: nested_sound_id (Gamma' Lambda : OutputCtx Atom) (a : Atom) : Derivable (@CS5ModalAxiom Atom) ((<Gamma', Lambda, .atom (.atom a)> : InputCtx Atom).fillLhs (.atom (.atom a))).fm
sorry_inventory.assumption: Assumes CS5ModalAxiom can derive `X.fm imp a` for the ctx.Lambda.fillLhs-built X at arbitrary chain depth (needed to necessitate through OutputCtx.fillRhs and conclude the id axiom's soundness).
sorry_inventory.why_deferred: The general-depth step needs a diamond-shedding fact (dia X imp X) that is not a CS5 theorem and is false in general (no dual of tBox for diamond exists). Concrete counterexample found: Gamma' := [], Lambda := [.empty, .empty] reduces the needed fact to `dia a imp a` for an arbitrary atom a, which fails in any non-degenerate frame. This is evidence of a likely encoding issue in id's fully-general (Gamma' Lambda : OutputCtx) signature in Rules.lean (Phase 9), not a proof this phase failed to find.
sorry_inventory.follow_up_task: Rules.lean id-signature review: restrict id's Lambda parameter, or re-derive id directly against a bare OutputCtx via .fillFull (mirroring Lemma 4.2's own scope) instead of routing through the general InputCtx split. Same follow-up as nested_sound_orL below.

sorry_inventory.statement: nested_sound_orL (ctx : InputCtx Atom) (A B : Proposition Atom) (hA : Derivable (@CS5ModalAxiom Atom) (ctx.fillLhs (.atom A)).fm) (hB : Derivable (@CS5ModalAxiom Atom) (ctx.fillLhs (.atom B)).fm) : Derivable (@CS5ModalAxiom Atom) (ctx.fillLhs (.atom (A.or B))).fm
sorry_inventory.assumption: Assumes CS5ModalAxiom can combine the two premises' dia-wrapped consequences into the disjunction's dia-wrapped consequence at arbitrary ctx.Lambda chain depth.
sorry_inventory.why_deferred: At ctx.Lambda-depth >= 2 this needs `dia (X or Y) imp (dia X or dia Y)` for arbitrary X, Y -- exactly `kdisj` (Intuitionistic/IS5.lean's axiom), which is deliberately absent from CS5ModalAxiom (an IS5-only addition, per this task's own research notes). Depth <= 1 is fully provable via orE alone with no diamond involved; only the general case is blocked. Same root cause as nested_sound_id (InputCtx.fillLhs's unbounded Lambda inserting an unremovable diamond past depth 1).
sorry_inventory.follow_up_task: Same Rules.lean follow-up as nested_sound_id -- both are instances of the same InputCtx.fillLhs unbounded-Lambda structural issue; a single follow-up task should address both.

summary: Phase 12 (Theorem 4.1, propositional and k cases, second of Stage D's three phases) landed 7 of 10 target case lemmas fully proven in Nested/Soundness.lean: nested_sound_botL (via a new cs5DerivDiaBotElim combinator, dia-bot-elim through efq+dia-mono+bDia), nested_sound_andL, nested_sound_andR, nested_sound_orRLeft, nested_sound_orRRight, nested_sound_contract (thin modus-ponens wrappers over Phase 11's Lemma 4.6/4.9 corollaries), and nested_sound_impR, which additionally RESOLVES Phase 11's deferred fillRhs-vs-fillFull bridging induction cleanly via tBox and curry/uncurry combinators (cs5DerivCurrySwapSchema, buildFullChain_imp_buildRhsChain, fillFull_imp_fillRhs) with no new axiom needed. nested_sound_id and nested_sound_orL are landed as two documented, tightly-scoped strategic sorries: this phase's investigation found a genuine mathematical obstruction (not merely missing machinery) affecting both -- InputCtx.fillLhs's unbounded Lambda chain inserts a diamond past depth 1 that CS5ModalAxiom cannot shed (no dual of tBox for diamond; orL's deep case additionally needs kdisj, an IS5-only axiom). A concrete counterexample for id is documented (Gamma'=[], Lambda=[.empty,.empty] reduces to needing `dia a imp a`), flagged as likely evidence of an encoding issue in Rules.lean's id constructor rather than a gap in this phase's proof search.
decisions_made: cs5DerivDiaBotElim (dia-bot proves bot) is a NEW combinator this phase, derived via efq (bot imp box-bot), dia-monotonicity (kdia), and bDia (dia-box-X imp X). It resolves botL's general-Lambda soundness, but is NOT a template that generalizes to id (bare-atom target) or orL (disjunction target): it works only because the target bot is absorbing under efq.

impR's fillRhs-vs-fillFull bridging is fully resolvable (contrary to how deeply Phase 11 flagged it): both OutputCtx.fillFull and OutputCtx.fillRhs bottom out through .box (never .dia) in their own recursions, so tBox (box-X imp X) reconciles the base-case box mismatch, and curry/uncurry (cs5DerivCurrySwapSchema) handles the singleton case. No new axiom was needed -- this is a materially easier case than id/orL, which route through .dia instead.

id and orL's general-Lambda soundness is genuinely blocked, not merely hard: multiple alternative proof strategies were tried (strengthening the inductive hypothesis to carry box-a or dia-a instead of bare a; using fourDia to collapse nested diamonds; using bBox/bDia/fourBox creatively) and all either reduce to the same unavailable diamond-shedding step or to a false base case. This is now a confirmed mathematical fact about CS5ModalAxiom's axiom set (verified against Intuitionistic/IS5.lean's kdisj addition), not an unexplored search space.

id's counterexample (Gamma'=[], Lambda=[.empty,.empty]) is evidence the Rules.lean id constructor's fully-general (Gamma' Lambda : OutputCtx) signature (Phase 9) may not correctly capture Figure 2's id axiom, which per Lemma 4.2 (already landed, Phase 11) treats its context as a bare OutputCtx via .fillFull, not the InputCtx split with two independently-free context parameters. This is flagged for a follow-up task/research pass, not fixed in this dispatch (Rules.lean is outside this phase's assigned file scope and is a preserved asset from Phase 9).
dead_ends: Strengthening nested_sound_id's target to L(a).fm imp (box a) fails at the base case (Lambda=[] needs a imp box-a, false in general).

Deriving dia(X or Y) imp (dia X or dia Y) from k/kdia/tBox/tDia/fourBox/fourDia/bBox/bDia alone was attempted via several routes (necessitation+kdia chains, bDia-mediated box-diamond roundtrips) -- none succeed; this matches Intuitionistic/IS5.lean's kdisj being a genuinely separate axiom addition over CS5ModalAxiom.

Bridging InputCtx.fillLhs to OutputCtx.fillFull via ctx.outputPruning (Gamma' ++ Lambda), analogous to impR's fillFull-vs-fillRhs bridge, does not work: fillLhs's box-wrapping structure (extra .box (Lambda.fillLhs Delta) pi layer) is not fm-equivalent to fillFull's structure even up to trivial top-insertion, confirmed by direct computation at Gamma'=[],Lambda=[] (fillLhs gives an extra box+top-implication layer that fillFull's identity case does not have).
